title: Integrated Protocol for Phytolith and Diatom Extraction from Carbonised Food Crusts
author: Robert C. Power
materials: The tube is vortexed for approximately 3 seconds.
It is then sonicated for about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Document and collect food crust
steps.instruction: Photograph the in‑situ food crust. Using a cleaned dental curette, dislodge carbonised crusts (preferably in chunks) onto creased weighing paper placed over smoothened tinfoil to catch spills. Transfer the material from the paper into pre‑labelled, pre‑weighed 1.5 ml plastic centrifuge tubes. Aim for 50–70 mg of crust (protocol works down to 5 mg, but samples <10 mg are impractical). If organic residue analysis is also required, store the sample in glass, foil, or plastic.

steps.title: Cool and reweigh combusted sample
steps.instruction: Allow the combusted sample to cool for approximately 60 minutes. Transfer the cooled material into new pre‑labelled, pre‑weighed 1.5 ml centrifuge tubes. Observe colour; a brown‑orange hue indicates clay richness. Weigh the tubes to record the combined soluble and insoluble fraction mass.

steps.title: Acid treatment and dilution
steps.instruction: Add 0.4–0.8 ml of hydrochloric acid (5–12 % v/v) to each tube; tap the tube sides to aid saturation of the ash. After the reaction ceases (a few minutes), dilute the mixture with water until the tube is full.

steps.title: Optional clay removal extraction
steps.instruction: If clay removal is required, after drying, follow a variant of the Rapid Phytolith Extraction method: weigh 20–50 mg of the extract and place it into a 0.5 ml conical plastic centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare phytolith/diatom slide sample
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1 mg of the extracted phytoliths and diatoms to a microscope slide. The weighed amount can be prepared in a sample boat or placed directly on the slide that has been zeroed on a balance.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash acid‑insoluble fraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 2000 × g for 10 minutes. Using a 3 ml plastic pipette, remove the supernatant and add water to the tube; repeat the wash (add water, centrifuge, remove supernatant) three times to fully eliminate residual acid.

steps.title: Dry acid‑insoluble fraction
steps.instruction: Place the tubes containing the acid‑insoluble fraction (AIF) in a drying oven set to 50 °C and dry for 48 hours.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and supernatant mounting
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the dried tube for 10 minutes at 5000 rpm. Pipette 50 µl of the resulting supernatant onto a glass microscope slide and cover with a 24 mm × 24 mm cover slip. The slide is now ready for micro‑remain counting.

steps.title: Optional charcoal oxidation with H₂O₂
steps.instruction: If substantial charcoal remains, add ~1 ml of 30 % hydrogen peroxide to the dry sample in the 1.5 ml tube while wearing safety gloves, allowing gases to escape. Incubate the tube in a 50 °C drying oven; as H₂O₂ decomposes, add more if needed. Degradation may take several days and can reduce articulated phytoliths. Remove remaining H₂O₂ by centrifugation or gravity sedimentation.

steps.title: Alternative SPT removal and drying
steps.instruction: Alternatively, remove the sodium polytungstate (SPT) by diluting the tube with water until full and centrifuging at 2000 × g for 10 minutes. Collect the waste supernatant for recycling (filtration and evaporation). After drying, the sample is ready for mounting and storage.

steps.title: Add sodium polytungstate solution
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl of sodium polytungstate solution (Na₆(H₂W₁₂O₄₀)·H₂O) with a specific gravity of 2.35 g cm⁻³ using a 100–1000 µl mechanical pipette.

steps.title: Transfer to labelled crucible
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample into a 20–50 ml crucible that has been labelled with a pencil and the label burned at 500 °C for 5 hours in a muffle oven. For samples >1 g, use a larger crucible to avoid anaerobic conditions.

steps.title: Place cover slip on sample
steps.instruction: Place a clean cover slip on the sample; a 22 mm × 22 mm slip is convenient for typical volumes.

steps.title: Apply Entellan mounting medium
steps.instruction: Add two drops of Entellan New™ mounting medium to the sample using a sterile disposable pipette, allowing the drops to run from the pipette shaft rather than the bulb.

steps.title: Mix and distribute particles
steps.instruction: Mix the Entellan and the extract powder on the slide with a disposable wooden cocktail stick to distribute phytoliths and diatoms evenly, especially for quantitative work.

steps.title: Cure slide in fume hood
steps.instruction: Allow the slide to cure flat in a fume hood. After about one day, an initial examination can be performed once the mounting medium has set at the cover‑slip edges. Complete drying may take up to two weeks.
